The '''Excellence class''',<ref name="excellenceclass">{{cite web |date=April 17, 2018 |title=Carnival not occupied with building world's largest cruise ship |url=https://www.ttgmedia.com/news/news/carnival-not-occupied-with-building-worlds-largest-cruise-ship-13868 |access-date=January 11, 2020 |website=TTG Media}}</ref><ref name="excellenceclass2">{{cite web |date=November 15, 2018 |title=Steel cut for Carnival Cruise Line's first Excellence-class ship |url=http://www.travelweekly.co.uk/articles/316905/steel-cut-for-carnival-cruise-lines-first-excellence-class-ship |access-date=May 29, 2019 |website=Travel Weekly}}</ref><ref name="excellenceclass3">{{cite web |date=January 5, 2020 |title=Mardi Gras delays not surprising but still costly for Carnival |url=https://www.travelweekly.com/Cruise-Travel/Mardi-Gras-delays-not-surprising-but-still-costly-for-Carnival |access-date=January 6, 2020 |website=Travel Weekly}}</ref> including the sub-classes '''Helios'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIDAnova |url=https://www.meyerwerft.de/en/meyerwerft_de/schiffe/kreuzfahrtschiffe/aida_cruises/n_n__1/n_n__2.jsp |access-date=May 3, 2019 |work=Meyer Werft}}</ref> and '''XL''' or '''Excel''',<ref name="xlclass">{{cite web |title=P&O Cruises and Cunard make 2022 single use plastics commitment |url=http://www.carnivalcorp.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=200767&p=irol-newsArticle&ID=2330312 |access-date=May 26, 2019 |website=Carnival Corporation}}</ref> is a class of cruise ships ordered by [[Carnival Corporation & plc]] for its [[subsidiary]] brands [[AIDA Cruises]], [[Costa Cruises]], [[P&O Cruises]] and [[Carnival Cruise Line]]. The ships are being constructed by [[Meyer Werft]] at their shipyard in [[Papenburg]], Germany, and [[Meyer Turku]] at their shipyard in [[Turku]], Finland. The first, {{ship||AIDAnova}}, entered service for AIDA Cruises in 2018.

== History ==
In March 2015, Carnival Corporation entered into a strategic partnership with Meyer Werft to build new ships between 2018 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.meyerwerft.de/en/meyerwerft_de/medien/presseticker/pressemitteilung_detail_20193.jsp|title=Carnival Corporation Enters into Strategic Partnerships to Add Nine Cruise Ships to its Fleet over a Four-Year Period Starting in 2019|date=March 24, 2015|access-date=January 2, 2017}}</ref> In June 2015, four ships were ordered for delivery between 2019 and 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.meyerturku.fi/en/meyerturku_com/media/presseticker/pressemitteilung_detailansicht_11672.jsp|title=Carnival Corporation orders two cruise ships from Meyer Turku|date=June 15, 2015|access-date=January 2, 2017|archive-date=September 25, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925170049/https://www.meyerturku.fi/en/meyerturku_com/media/presseticker/pressemitteilung_detailansicht_11672.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="nextgeneration">{{cite web|url=http://www.meyerwerft.de/en/meyerwerft_de/medien/presseticker/pressemitteilung_detail_20303.jsp|title=Carnival Corporation Finalizes Contract with Meyer Werft to Build Four Next-Generation Cruise Ships|date=June 15, 2015|access-date=January 2, 2017}}</ref>  In September 2016, three more ships were ordered for [[Carnival Cruise Line]] and [[P&O Cruises]] for delivery in 2020 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.meyerwerft.de/en/meyerwerft_de/medien/presseticker/pressemitteilung_detail_23117.jsp|title=Carnival Corporation to Build Three New LNG-Powered Cruise Ships with Meyer Werft and Meyer Turku|date=September 6, 2016|access-date=January 2, 2017}}</ref> In February 2024, Carnival Cruise Line placed an order for another Excellence class ship for delivery in 2027.

The Excellence class are the first cruise ships in the world to be dual fueled by [[liquefied natural gas]] (LNG) and traditional [[fuel oil]], which is intended to make them more environmentally friendly than traditional, [[Diesel fuel|diesel-powered]] ships.<ref name="nextgeneration"/> Each ship is expected to cost $950 million.<ref name="orderbook">{{cite web|url=https://www.cruiseindustrynews.com/cruise-news/cruise-ship-orderbook.html|title=Cruise ship ordeerbook|date=6 January 2011|access-date=February 25, 2017}}</ref>

The first four ships in the class suffered delivery delays. The delays of ''AIDAnova'', ''Costa Smeralda'' and ''Mardi Gras'' were attributed to the ships being the first to be fueled by LNG, design complexities, difficulties coordinating subcontractors, and the large size of the ships.<ref name="excellenceclass3"/> The delay of ''Iona'' was due to a temporary suspension of operations by P&O Cruises, and slower construction progress, in response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="maidendelayed">{{cite web|title=P&O Cruises Reveals Maiden Voyage of New Ship Iona Will be Delayed|url=https://www.cruisecritic.co.uk/news/5232/|last=Spencer|first=Kerry|publisher=Cruise Critic|date=March 30, 2020|access-date=March 31, 2020|archive-date=January 16, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116183614/https://www.cruisecritic.co.uk/news/5232/|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Mardi Gras'' was later delayed until 2021, also due to the pandemic.<ref name="mardigras2021">{{cite web|title=Another delay for Carnival's Mardi Gras ship|url=https://www.travelweekly.com/Cruise-Travel/Another-delay-for-Carnival-Mardi-Gras-ship|last=Limone|first=Jerry|publisher=Travel Weekly|date=July 7, 2020|access-date=July 7, 2020}}</ref>
